title: Aletheia v2 ground-up architecture investigation
question: How should Aletheia v2 be structured from the ground up to deliver bounded, evidence-correct, auditable agentic research while earning its complexity against a strong single-agent baseline?

conclusion.default: bounded single-lead research with controller-owned state, finite envelope, typed evidence and claims, and explicit terminal states
conclusion.opt_in: audited source-separated investigation under a predeclared plan and global budget
not_recommended: patching the v0.5 filesystem blackboard into a larger swarm
platform/framework expansion before a bounded vertical slice and matched evaluation

method.channel_health: 12 of 13 core channels live; Brave degraded without API key
method.raw_research_policy: raw retrieval bodies and mutable run state are intentionally gitignored

key_evidence.role: reproduced v0.5 source identity, state integrity, resource, and evaluation limitations
corrected controlled comparison; 11-11 factual-rubric tie with unequal read assignments
project-authored claim/evidence, stopping, and evaluation design hypotheses
experimental mechanism inventory and unpromoted status

limitations: No v2 implementation exists, so this is not a v2 performance benchmark.
Current evidence does not establish a cross-vendor quality, latency, or cost ranking.
The one controlled local comparison was source-frozen, small, and not fully resource-matched.
Channel health is point-in-time, and Brave was unavailable without a key.
An append-only ledger is not administrator-proof absent deployment-specific external anchoring.
non_changes: No production runtime files are intentionally changed by this dossier.
Existing unrelated worktree changes are preserved and excluded from this audit commit.
